name: Liqimsa
body:
LIQIMSA
CR 9

This wrinkly gray-skinned pachyderm has discolored tusks tipped in reddish brown stains and a cruel but keen eyes with a glint of cunning.

XP 6,400
N Huge magical beast
Init +1; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +12
Aura frightful presence (30 ft., DC 18)

DEFENSE

AC 20, touch 9, flat-footed 19 (+1 Dex, +11 natural, -2 size)
hp 126 (12d10+60)
Fort +13, Ref +9, Will +7

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee gore +22 (2d8+11/19-20), slam +21 (2d6+11)
Ranged rock +12 (1d12+11)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 10 ft. (15 ft. with trunk)
Special Attacks humanoid hunter, rock throwing (30 ft.), taste for vengeance, trample (2d8+16, DC 27), trampling charge

STATISTICS

Str 32, Dex 12, Con 21, Int 9, Wis 12, Cha 15
Base Atk +12; CMB +25; CMD 36 (40 vs. trip)
Feats Improved Critical (gore), Intimidating Prowess, Iron Will, Power Attack, Weapon Focus (gore)
Skills Intimidate +14, Perception +12, Survival +5
Languages Common

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Humanoid Hunter (Ex)

A liqisma gains a +2 competence bonus on attack and damage rolls and Intimidate, Perception, and Survival checks made against humanoids.

Taste for Vengeance (Ex)

If a liqisma takes damage, it gains a +1 morale bonus on attack and damage rolls against its attacker until the end of its next turn.

Trampling Charge (Ex)

When the liqisma moves at least 20 feet as part of a charge and hits with its gore, it can attempt a bull rush or trip combat maneuver against its target as a swift action.

If the maneuver succeeds, the target takes 2d8+15 bludgeoning damage (DC 26 Reflex half). The save DC is Strength-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm plains
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure none

These creatures resemble nothing so much as ordinary bull elephants, but they have a vile taste for humanoid flesh.

They are intelligent and have the power of speech, which they use to bluster and threatened and demand a tribute of sacrifices to slake their bloody hunger. They can subsist just enough to avoid utter starvation if forced to eat grass, leaves, and similar vegetation, but they despise the taste, and even the flesh of animals does not truly satisfy them. They are cunning enough to uproot and hurl trees and rocks with their prehensile trunks, though not with great accuracy.
